description: A value the accidental POSIX reading matches is refused here as outside the dialect.
descriptor: { descriptor_version: "1.0", root: { type: "object", children: { a: { type: "string", pattern: "[[:alpha:]]+" } } } }

divergence.note: docs/grammars.md §1.2 and §1.3 fix which layer reports each regex construct, and §1.2 states that the two implementations can name the same problem at different layers while the outcome (refused, named, never guessed at) does not differ. This is a documented, intentional divergence from the executed baseline under that rule (SPEC.md amendment 26), not a baseline defect.  Both engines read [[:alpha:]] as a class of the literal characters bracket, colon, a, l, p, h plus a stray bracket, so the pattern silently means something other than what it appears to say. Here the pattern itself is named as outside the dialect before any match; the baseline has no dialect gate and accepts the value this accidental reading matches.
